issues.detail: Does not address error scenarios or edge cases such as missing user information, ambiguous requirements, or non-standard reporting structures.

scenarios.name: new-role-job-posting
scenarios.rationale: Response B comprehensively covers all seven required sections (About Company, About Role, What You'll Do, What We're Looking For with separate Required/Nice to Have, What We Offer, How to Apply, EEO), uses consistent active 'you' language, and provides exactly 8 well-structured responsibilities starting with action verbs that explain impact ('Own the roadmap,' 'Define product strategy,' 'Partner to unblock expansion opportunities'); Response A declines entirely as out-of-project-scope, meeting zero rubric requirements.

scenarios.name: inclusive-job-rewrite
scenarios.rationale: Both responses appropriately request the job posting first, but Response B more precisely aligns with the rubric by specifying the exact 4-6 requirement range (vs A's 3-5), providing concrete linguistic examples ('you'll build' vs 'must own'), and offering more detailed rewriting guidance; neither explicitly commits to X+ years formatting with equivalent-experience clauses or an explicit equal opportunity statement, which are two of the four rubric requirements.

scenarios.name: job-board-variants
scenarios.rationale: Both appropriately request source material before creating variants, but Response B explicitly commits to each rubric requirement (150-word HN format with salary/tech upfront, LinkedIn with company branding, detailed careers page) while Response A characterizes platforms more vaguely; Response B also provides more systematic information gathering with both detailed-field and paste-existing-description pathways.
